Problem 525. Reading a layered map legend (A1)
A map legend translates symbols into properties. One location may have several properties at the same time.

Legend: tree=forest, wavy line=river, double line=road, arch=bridge, square=village, triangle=hill. Cells: A1 has forest, road; A2 has bridge, river; B1 has bridge, forest, river, road; B2 has road, village. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.

A cell satisfies the task only if it has every required attribute. Extra attributes do not disqualify it unless the task says so. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Which cell or cells satisfy all of these conditions: river, road? Explain by intersecting the clues. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?

1. Convert the requested symbols into the attribute set ['river', 'road']. 2. Check each cell for every required attribute. 3. The matching set is ['B1']. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Map reading often means intersecting clues rather than recognizing one symbol in isolation.
Set model; each cell has an attribute set; return cells whose set is a superset of the required set.
Problem 526. Choosing a safe settlement site: case 1
Human settlements depend on several factors at once. Some conditions may be compulsory while others are preferences.

Candidate sites: Site A: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=2; Site B: water=yes, road=no, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=4; Site C: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=yes, nearby farmland score=4; Site D: water=no, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=6. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 12 members, requires at least 7 present for quorum, and 11 are present.

A valid site must have water, road access, and must not be in the flood zone. Among valid sites, choose the one with the highest farmland score. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Which site should be selected under the stated mandatory conditions and preference rule? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?

1. Separate mandatory conditions from the preference. 2. Filtering by water, road, and flood safety leaves ['Site A']. 3. Compare only the farmland scores of feasible sites: Site A=2. 4. Site A has the best score among valid sites. Cross-domain check: compare 11 with 7; 11≥7 is true.
Site A. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
Good decisions first satisfy hard constraints and only then optimize among the remaining options.
Constraint-satisfaction problem followed by a score maximization over feasible options.

Problem 531. Terrain and travel cost from Riverbend
Equal-looking distances can require different effort because terrain differs. A simple cost model makes that effect explicit.

Terrain energy costs per segment: {'plain': 1, 'forest': 2, 'hill': 3, 'marsh': 4}. Three routes from Riverbend to Alder: R1=['plain', 'hill', 'plain']; R2=['forest', 'forest', 'plain']; R3=['plain', 'marsh']. The traveler can spend at most 10 energy units.
The energy of a route is the sum of its terrain costs. A route above the energy limit is infeasible. Among feasible routes, minimize energy.
Which route is feasible and uses the least energy?
1. Compute route totals: R1=5, R2=5, R3=5. 2. Discard any total above 10. 3. The smallest remaining total is R1=5.
Relief changes the cost of movement; “shortest” and “easiest” are not automatically the same.
Weighted paths with a feasibility budget; sum costs and choose the minimum feasible path.
